card.statement: Inspect the deployed launch flags, checkout, patch, and container first: the supplied profile says DSpark k5 has adaptive verification disabled, while its CSV says DSpark is off. If verification is inactive and the DeepSeek-specific graph safety conditions are present or can be qualified, enable adaptive verification while retaining draft k5. The proposed mechanism is to spend less target verification work when a full drafted block is unlikely to be useful. This is a transfer inference, not an observed B200 benefit. The B300 concurrent-prefill failure makes mixed-batch graph eligibility a prerequisite, and the B200 tuning PR favors fixed k5. Advance only if same-topology tests improve SLO-qualified cost and throughput without sampling, rollback, or latency regressions.
card.observed_bottleneck: Unknown on the target deployment. No supplied result isolates verification cost on 8×B200.
card.mechanism: Adaptive verification may reduce target work while keeping the draft width at k5; mixed prefill must avoid unsafe FULL graph capture.
card.proposed_change: After flag and code inspection, qualify graph-safe mixed prefill and decode, then toggle enable_adaptive_verification with draft k5 fixed. Keep any safety patch separate from the toggle.
card.code_surface: Deployed launch configuration; DSpark adaptive verification; DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse attention metadata builders and CUDA graph eligibility.
card.applicability: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8×B200, 2×DEP4 baseline, agent-f75 and fixed Mooncake traces. Transfer from B300 and GLM is unproven.
card.predicted_direction: Possible increase in SLO-qualified goodput per GPU dollar and decrease in cost per successful million output tokens; size and even sign are unknown.

experiment.control: Same frozen 2×DEP4 topology with static k5; also static k2 and no speculation.
experiment.treatment: Graph-safe adaptive verification with draft k5, with safety changes already fixed in every relevant arm.
experiment.metrics: Both Mooncake custom and AIPerf SLO-qualified goodput scorers; GPU-dollar cost; cost per successful million output tokens; TTFT and E2E p95/p99; ITL by output-length cohort; acceptance, errors, and correctness.
experiment.supports_if: Safety and correctness pass, and a prespecified repeatable improvement of at least the proposed 5% engineering threshold appears in target cost-throughput metrics without violating latency SLOs.
experiment.rejects_if: Mixed-batch safety or exact sampling and KV rollback fails, or qualified adaptive k5 cannot outperform the strongest eligible static comparator under the prespecified decision rule.

experiment.cost: Cheap read-only flag and code inspection first; then targeted safety qualification and a bounded same-topology GPU sweep. No GPU execution in this session.

card.revision_reason: The B200 fixed-k5 recommendation and B300 illegal-memory report make this a conditional safety-qualified test, not an assumed activation gain.

task_value.rationale: The cheap flag inspection can resolve whether activation is a real baseline delta: the brief says “CSV dspark_config off contradicts profile on; runtime flags not inspected.” The same-topology experiment targets the required cost and latency metrics. The target verification bottleneck and benefit remain unknown.

correctness_and_safety.rationale: The proposal retains draft k5 and calls for sampling, KV rollback, and graph-safe decode checks. Safety is unqualified: issue #59970 reports “IMA within 1 min at c96 (4/4)” on B300, while PR #59986 says its end-to-end reproducer was “Not run.” Neither establishes safety on this B200 deployment.

causal_test.rationale: It compares adaptive k5 with static k5, static k2, and no speculation on one frozen topology and fixed traces. It specifies both goodput scorers, TTFT/E2E tails, ITL length cohorts, correctness, and a separate safety change. The reported R7b and R10 results cannot isolate speculation because their layouts and load points differ.

implementation_evidence.rationale: The supplied issue and PR bodies identify relevant graph builders and a proposed safety change, but deployed code and flags have not been inspected. PR #62541 says B200 qualified lanes use “enable_adaptive_verification:false”; that author claim supports testing the choice, not assuming activation helps.

objections: Author-reported negative evidence is stronger than the draft’s short quotes convey: #59970 says “Throughput was the same within noise” for its workaround comparison, and #62541 reports fixed full-block verification in qualified B200 lanes.
The #59970 failure occurred on 2×B300 with TP2 and a different workload; transfer to 8×B200 is unknown.
The claimed safety fix is an open PR whose B300 end-to-end reproducer was not run. Exact sampling distribution and KV rollback on the proposed build are unknown.
PR #45963 concerns batch-local dynamic draft K under DP. Keeping draft k5 fixed avoids that documented divergence mechanism, but does not establish adaptive verification safety.
review.required_revision: Keep this as the first, deferred hypothesis. Inspect effective flags and freeze the checkout, patch, and container; establish graph-safe concurrent-prefill behavior and correctness before the bounded same-topology performance comparison. State #59970’s throughput result and #62541’s fixed-k5 choice explicitly.

card.statement: Consider verification-cost calibration only if deployed inspection shows adaptive verification is eligible, graph safety is qualified, and its cost model uses profiling shapes above the reachable decode ceiling. A B200 issue reports that such shapes can be mistaken for uniform decode; an open PR proposes schedulable mixed prefill and decode tails. Port or enable that behavior only if absent from the frozen runtime, and retain the current captured decode shapes. The mechanism is a more faithful cost estimate for the batches that actually occur, which might change adaptive decisions under prefill pressure. No supplied evidence shows that calibration improves serving performance on this target; if the behavior already exists or decisions do not change, stop.
card.observed_bottleneck: Unknown. The supplied B200 issue identifies an invalid profiling shape, not a measured target serving bottleneck.
card.mechanism: Scheduler-reachable mixed-batch profiling could correct verification-cost estimates used by an eligible adaptive policy.
card.proposed_change: Inspect whether #54077 or equivalent behavior is present. If absent and relevant, use explicit mixed decode/prefill tail splits above the k5 decode ceiling, preserving captured graph shapes; isolate this change from graph safety and adaptive activation.
card.code_surface: AdaptiveVerificationManager batches_to_profile, dummy-run scheduling and context, model runner profiling, and cost selection.
card.applicability: Conditional on an active adaptive policy and a reachable tail-shape mismatch in the frozen B200 runtime. Effect on target workload is unknown.
card.predicted_direction: Potentially better policy decisions and SLO-qualified cost-throughput; no directional benefit is established without decision and cost traces.

card.revision_reason: The supplied B200 profiling issue gives a concrete mechanism, while the open PR and absent serving evaluation require an upstream-presence gate and conditional selection.

task_value.rationale: Issue #54046 describes a concrete profiling mismatch: “Anything the profiler measures above 1024 tokens cannot be decode” for its k7, seq128 example. Whether the frozen k5 runtime has the behavior, reaches relevant tail shapes, changes decisions, or improves target cost and latency is unknown. The proposed code-presence and shape checks are cheap.

correctness_and_safety.rationale: The proposal preserves draft k5 and makes graph safety and adaptive eligibility prerequisites. PR #54077 claims it changes startup profiling shapes and “does not modify sampling or verification kernels,” but target sampling, rollback, and concurrent-prefill safety have not been qualified.

causal_test.rationale: The treatment changes profiling alone after activation and safety are frozen. It checks reachable shapes, cost estimates, and decisions before a bounded serving comparison with fixed traces, both scorers, latency tails, ITL cohorts, and correctness. The second-stage comparison remains conditional on the first hypothesis producing an eligible adaptive baseline.

implementation_evidence.rationale: PR #54077 supplies a specific claimed implementation: “profiles tail samples as schedulable mixed decode/prefill batches,” with reported regression tests. It also says “A full DSpark model-serving evaluation was not run.” The pinned runtime’s code path and any equivalent upstream behavior remain uninspected.

objections: The 1024-token ceiling is from a k7, seq128 configuration; the target k5 ceiling must be calculated from resolved runtime limits and checked against actual scheduled shapes.
PR #54077’s reported tests used an RTX 5090. Its serving effect on the specified 8×B200 workload is unknown.
A corrected profile may leave policy decisions unchanged. No target effect size or active verification-cost bottleneck is supplied.
DScale’s reported A100 TP1 gains and EVICT’s estimator limitations are context, not evidence that this vLLM port improves B200 serving.
review.required_revision: Retain only as a conditional second hypothesis. First establish adaptive eligibility and safety, inspect the pinned profiler for equivalent behavior, then verify a reachable shape mismatch and changed decisions before any performance sweep.
